## Where the author is lost

Short answer: it isn't lost anywhere — it's **never captured**, and the floor is the schema. There's no author on a comment at any of the four layers, so there's nothing to leak.

**1. Entity — the root cause.** `src/article/comment.entity.ts:5-15` has exactly `id`, `body`, and `@ManyToOne article`. No `author` column, no relation to `UserEntity`. With `synchronize: true` the `comment` table has no `authorId` column at all. Everything below is downstream of this.

**2. Controller drops an identity it already has.** `src/article/article.controller.ts:77`:
```ts
async createComment(@Param('slug') slug, @Body('comment') commentData: CreateCommentDto)
```
No `@User()` param. The caller *is* authenticated — `POST articles/:slug/comments` is in the middleware list (`src/article/article.module.ts:28`) and `req.user` is populated at `src/user/auth.middleware.ts:24`. The handler simply never reads it.

**3. Service can't receive it either.** `src/article/article.service.ts:101-112` — `addComment(slug, commentData)` takes no user argument, and the construction is `comment.body = commentData.body` (`:104-105`). The DTO (`src/article/dto/create-comment.ts:1-3`) is `{ body }` only.

**4. Read path and the typed contract have no author.** `findComments()` (`article.service.ts:165-168`) returns `article.comments`, which loads fine — the relation is `{eager: true}` (`article.entity.ts:40`) — but each row is only `id`/`body`. And `CommentsRO`'s element type is literally `interface Comment { body: string }` (`src/article/article.interface.ts:3-5`). So `GET /api/articles/:slug/comments` yields `{comments: [{id, body}]}` and the client's `comment.author.username` is `undefined` → blank name.

## One extra bug on the same symptom

`addComment()` returns `{article}` (`article.service.ts:111`, typed `Promise<ArticleRO>`) and the controller passes it straight through (`article.controller.ts:78`). The spec's `POST /articles/:slug/comments` returns `{comment}`. So a client that posts a comment and renders the response optimistically gets `undefined` at the first hop, before any refetch — same blank-name symptom, different cause. That's LESSONS.md:49-57 (wrong envelope, not a missing one).

Also missing from the same entity: the spec's `comment.createdAt`/`updatedAt`.

## Why this matters beyond the display bug

`CURRENT_FOCUS.md:10-12` already flags this relation as the blocker for ownership checks on `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` — you can't 403 a non-author when the record has no author. One schema change unblocks both.

*Not read:* `prisma/` (per `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:22-24` it's not the production path), and the test files.

Want me to draft the fix? It touches the entity, the service signature, the controller's `@User()`, and `CommentsRO` — and per your focus doc the ownership half is design-first, so I'd keep this change to producing the author and leave the 403 separate.
